transcript.text: dryer drum wont turn but i can here it running, hotpiont. clothes just sit there

A Hotpoint dryer that sounds like it's running while the drum just sits there is most often a snapped or slipped-off drive belt. - An overloaded drum, or one heavy item like a duvet or rug, stopping it turning.
• A failed motor start capacitor. This is likely if what you're hearing is more of a steady hum than the motor actually spinning.
• Less often, the belt tension (jockey) pulley, worn drum rollers, or something jammed. 1. Check the load. If it was very full or a single bulky item, take some out and try a short programme. If the drum turns now, it was just overloaded.
2. Unplug the dryer, empty it, and turn the drum slowly by hand. - If it spins round very easily with almost no resistance, that points to the belt being broken or off. - If it feels stiff or stuck, that points to the rollers or something jammed rather than the belt. - If it feels normal (a bit of drag), the belt may be intact.
3. Listen when it's switched on. A motor that's whirring and running is different from a low hum with no spin. A hum with the drum free by hand points to the start capacitor rather than the belt. If it does turn out to be the belt, it's a common, inexpensive repair. Fitting one means taking the back or top panel off and getting it round the motor and tension pulley. Some confident owners do it, but many people get an engineer in. A capacitor or motor problem is more of an engineer job. One other thing: some older Hotpoint (and Indesit, Creda, Swan and Proline) dryers were covered by a fire-safety modification programme. It's worth checking yours on Hotpoint's dryer safety checker or GOV.UK product safety alerts, especially before any repair. So, when you turn the empty drum by hand with it unplugged, does it spin very easily, feel normal, or feel stiff?
just tried it unplugged and the drum spins really easily with almost no resistance. also heard a twang then a thud yesterday mid cycle and a bit of a rubber smell at the time

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. That pattern is about as clear as these get. A twang and a thud mid-cycle, a whiff of hot rubber at the same moment, the motor still running and now a drum that spins round with almost no resistance all point strongly to the drive belt having snapped or come off. The belt is what connects the motor to the drum, so without it the motor runs happily and the drum just sits there. I'd put this at high confidence. The capacitor and a seized drum are now unlikely, because the motor is clearly running and the drum isn't stiff. The rubber smell is the reason this needs an engineer before the dryer is used again. A belt usually smells like that as it slips and snaps. But a burning smell in a dryer always needs a proper look, because the same smell can come from a seized jockey pulley, belt debris sitting near the heater or motor, or lint build-up. Please leave it unplugged and don't run it, even to test it, until a qualified engineer has checked it. What the engineer would typically do:
1. Take the back or top panel off and confirm the belt is broken or off. That suggests the diagnosis.
2. Check the jockey (tension) pulley turns freely and isn't worn. A seized or wobbly pulley is a common reason belts snap, and it should be dealt with at the same time.
3. Clear out any shredded belt and lint inside the casing, and check around the heater and motor for heat damage. If it is just the belt, possibly with the pulley, it's normally one of the cheaper dryer repairs and well worth doing rather than replacing the dryer, unless the machine is very old or has other problems. It's also worth having the engineer confirm the dryer isn't one that needs the Hotpoint safety modification while they're there. If you can send the model number, I can tell you a bit more about what's typical for that range.
